findings.body: Changing `openhuman_core::openhuman as oh` to `openhuman_core as oh` shifts the `oh` prefix from the `openhuman` submodule to the crate root. The unchanged usages (e.g. `oh::agent::stop_hooks::...`) must therefore resolve relative to `openhuman_core`'s root, not to `openhuman_core::openhuman`. If `agent` (or `stop_hooks`) is only exposed under the `openhuman` submodule, this breaks compilation of this module. Confirm that `openhuman_core::agent::stop_hooks` is a valid path before merging.
findings.existing_code:
use openhuman_core as oh;

use oh::agent::stop_hooks::{StopDecision, StopHook, TurnState};
findings.title: Verify agent::stop_hooks resolves from the crate root after re-aliasing

value.summary: The PR re-aliases the `oh` import from `openhuman_core::openhuman` to the crate root `openhuman_core`; all subsequent `oh::agent::stop_hooks` references now resolve against the crate root rather than the `openhuman` submodule. I cannot verify the crate's module layout from the diff alone, so I can only flag the resolution risk at low confidence.
